subject: Cygnus POC: KV cache TTL causing stale prefixes / SDK flag request
messages:
From: Anna Koval <anna@cygnus.ai>
To: Elliot Price <elliot@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC: unexpected model state / stale prefixes when reusing convo

Hi Elliot / Marissa,

Quick report from our engineers running the Cygnus POC on the hosted API: when clients reuse conversation prefixes across short-lived sessions, sometimes the model returns answers that include previous session context (stale prefixes). It looks like token latencies are fine, but the responses include unrelated facts from an earlier demo. We attached a short log and a minimal prompt repro.

What we tried: resetting conversation id, but some clients still attach the same client-side request id and we suspect the server-side kv-cache is reusing keys. Can you confirm whether there is a per-request TTL on the KV cache or a way to force zero-cache for a single request from the SDK?

Attachments: cygnus-kvcache-sample.log, repro-prompt.json

This is blocking our next demo (we have a renewal discussion next week). Appreciate quick guidance.

Thanks,
Anna
Customer Success Engineer
Cygnus AI

----

From: Elliot Price <elliot@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-17T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: POC: unexpected model state / stale prefixes when reusing convo

Marissa / eng / product — forwarding Anna's note from Cygnus. TL;DR: they see cross-session leakage when reuse happens; suspect kv-cache keying + TTL.

Asks:
- Priority triage from runtime: can we confirm whether cached KV entries are scoped by any stable client identifier that could persist across sessions?
- Short-term mitigation: is there an API header or SDK flag we can recommend to disable caching per-request?
- Product: should we expose cache_ttl / cache_scope from SDK? If so, is that a quick add?

Customer impact: renewal at risk next week if demos keep showing stale state. They gave us logs and a minimal repro (attached).

Can we get a plan/ETA today?

Thanks,
Elliot

----

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-17T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: POC: unexpected model state / stale prefixes when reusing convo

Thanks for the ping and the logs. Quick triage notes:
- Initial read: behaviour matches a kv-cache keying edge where the request fingerprint (used to index cached KV) includes a client-supplied id that isn't being namespaced by session. If the same client-id appears across sessions, cached prefixes can be reused.
- I replicated a similar pattern locally with the repro prompt — attached minimal run shows cached prefix being applied when client-id is identical.

Immediate mitigation options we can advise the customer:
1) SDK header: they can set x-redwood-cache-disable: true (temporary; we can honor in hosted plane). This will force no KV cache lookup for that request.
2) Workaround: ensure clients rotate the client request id per session, or include a session nonce in the prompt.

Longer term: we should add a runtime config to namespace cache keys by request_id + session_id and expose a per-request cache_ttl parameter.

Action items for us:
- Need the exact repro-prompt.json (they attached; good).
- Can the customer provide a short request trace with request-id headers? That will let me confirm key generation.
- If Cygnus wants, I can enable honor-x-cache-disable flag for their org in hosted for 30 days as an exception while we ship a proper fix. That requires approvals (security + billing).

Dev
Senior Engineer, Runtime

----

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Anna Koval <anna@cygnus.ai>, Elliot Price <elliot@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-18T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC: unexpected model state / stale prefixes when reusing convo

Hi Anna — looping you in with a short repro and a suggested short-term client change. We've attached repro-prompt.json with two minimal examples: one that reproduces the stale prefix when client-id is constant, and one that avoids it when a session nonce is appended.

Temporary steps you can do now (no server change):
- Add a 6-char random session nonce to the conversation id or include as the first token in the prompt. That will break the cache key collision and prevent reusing prefixes.
- If you prefer a server-side toggle, we can flip x-redwood-cache-disable for your org while we ship a proper fix.

We're starting a runtime task (SUP-5124) to:
- ensure cache keys include session nonce when present
- add per-request cache_ttl support (API + SDK)
- add an honor list for x-redwood-cache-disable for orgs under POC exceptions

Expect timeline: small canary fix for cache namespacing in 2 sprints (target: 2025-06-05 canary), and API/SDK param in 3-4 sprints. I'll update SUP-5124 with concrete PRs.

Karthik
Staff Sales Engineer

----

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Elliot Price <elliot@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Anna Koval <anna@cygnus.ai>
Date: 2025-05-19T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC: unexpected model state / stale prefixes when reusing convo

Thanks all — good notes. For internal prioritization and customer communication:
- Product ask: expose per-request cache controls in SDK (cache_ttl, cache_scope: [session, request, org], and a cache_disable boolean). This should be an SDK-first feature with a thin API param that maps to an existing runtime header.
- Exception: I support making a temporary org-level toggle for Cygnus (30 days) so their demos are clean while we implement the fix. Marissa, please confirm if Cygnus wants us to enable the toggle ASAP.
- Timeline: Dev/Karthik estimate suggests canary by 2025-06-05 for namespacing. SDK param will follow; I propose we target SDK PRs in the sprint that starts 2025-06-08.

Next steps:
1) Marissa to confirm customer preference (session nonce vs server toggle).
2) Dev to draft the org-toggle change request for security + billing (I will shepherd approvals).
3) Karthik to update SUP-5124 with the repro and link to HubSpot record.
4) Product to draft a brief note for the customer documenting temporary and permanent mitigations.

Marissa — can you confirm by EOD 2025-05-19 whether we should flip the toggle? If yes, Laura will start the approval.

Thanks,
Laura
Product Manager
